questions.question: The number of live births per thousand people per year is called:
questions.solution: (d) Natality. Natality (birth rate) is the number of births per 1000 individuals per year.

questions.question: The structure that lies at the junction of the choroid and the iris and is itself a part of the choroid is called:
questions.solution: (a) Ciliary body. The ciliary body adjusts the lens for accommodation and produces aqueous humour.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Seminal vesicles pour an alkaline secretion into the semen as it passes through the ureter.
Reason (R): The female vagina is acidic and needs to be neutralized for sperm survival.
questions.solution: (b) (A) is false and (R) is true.. (A) is false: the secretion is added as semen passes through the ejaculatory duct, not the ureter. (R) is true.

questions.question: The hormone that induces vigorous contractions of the uterus in a pregnant mother is:
questions.solution: (c) Oxytocin. Oxytocin stimulates uterine muscle contraction during childbirth.

questions.question: A scientist wanted to conduct a genetic experiment on mice. He cut the tails of all the mice and made them reproduce. What will be the phenotype of the offsprings?

options.a: All the offsprings will be tailless.
options.b: There will be a mix of tailed and tailless offsprings.
options.c: All the offsprings will have tails.
options.d: Tail of the offsprings cannot be predicted.

questions.solution: (c) All the offsprings will have tails.. Tail cutting is an acquired trait affecting somatic cells, not germ cells, so it is not inherited.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A turgid plant cell is in a balanced state.
Reason (R): In a turgid cell, turgor pressure and wall pressure are equal and in the same direction.
questions.solution: (a) (A) is true and (R) is false.. (A) is true: no net water movement. (R) is false: turgor pressure and wall pressure are equal but act in opposite directions.

questions.question: The optimum temperature for photosynthesis is:
questions.solution: (d) 25 - 35°C. Photosynthesis is optimum at 25-35°C.

concepts: monohybrid cross inference of parental genotype
questions.question: Ajay and Vijay are siblings. Ajay can roll his tongue while Vijay cannot. What is the genotype of their parents?

options.a: Both the parents are homozygous dominant.
options.b: Both the parents are homozygous recessive.
options.c: One parent is homozygous dominant, and the other is homozygous recessive.
options.d: Both the parents are heterozygous dominant.

questions.solution: (d) Both the parents are heterozygous dominant.. Tongue rolling is dominant; Vijay is recessive (two recessive alleles), so each parent must carry one recessive allele yet roll the tongue, i.e. both are heterozygous.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Deficiency of antidiuretic hormone causes an increase in urination.
Reason (R): Antidiuretic hormone acts on the kidney to reabsorb water from the kidney tubules.
questions.solution: (c) Both (A) and (R) are true.. ADH promotes water reabsorption; deficiency means more water is lost as urine.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: A phase of cell division where the spindle fibres disappear is:
questions.solution: (a) Telophase. In telophase the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear and spindle fibres disappear.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Arachnoid layer helps in speeding up the transmission of nerve impulses along the axons.
Reason (R): Axon endings at the synapse secrete acetylene.
questions.solution: (d) Both (A) and (R) are false.. (A) false: arachnoid is a meninx; the myelin sheath speeds up impulses. (R) false: the neurotransmitter is acetylcholine.

questions.question: Many nuclear power plants are constructed near water sources. They use water for cooling their machinery and release it back into the water stream. Identify the kind of pollution caused.
questions.solution: (d) Thermal pollution. Release of heated water raises the temperature of the water body: thermal pollution.

concepts: rods and rhodopsin in night vision
questions.question: Owls are nocturnal animals. They are active at night and hunt small animals for food. Owls have large eyes and can see well at night. This is due to:
questions.solution: (c) Rods and Rhodopsin. Rods with rhodopsin give vision in dim light.

questions.question:
Sunil tried to match the tropic movements in plants with the stimulus they respond to. The tabulation is given below:
P: Thigmotropism - Touch
Q: Geotropism - Water
R: Chemotropism - Chemicals
S: Phototropism - Gravity
Identify the correct pair:
questions.solution: (a) P and R. Thigmotropism-touch (P) and chemotropism-chemicals (R) are the correct pairs. The paper prints options (a) and (d) identically, so both are marked correct.

questions.question: Observe the following picture, identify the defect and the cause of the defect.

options.a: Simple goitre, under secretion of thyroxine.
options.b: Ex-ophthalmic goitre, over secretion of thyroxine.
options.c: Simple goitre, over secretion of thyroxine.
options.d: Ex-ophthalmic goitre, under secretion of thyroxine.

questions.solution: (b) Ex-ophthalmic goitre, over secretion of thyroxine. Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is caused by hypersecretion of thyroid hormone, with bulging eyes.

questions.question: What is Micturition? Explain.
questions.solution: Micturition (urination) is the process of expelling urine from the urinary bladder through the urethra to the outside of the body. It is regulated by the nervous system and smooth muscles in the bladder and urethra.

marking_points.point: Expulsion of urine from the bladder through the urethra, controlled by nerves and smooth muscles

questions.solution: Any solid or liquid waste generated during diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals. Examples: used needles, syringes, cotton swabs, body organs, blood, tissues.

marking_points.point: Urethra: expels urine (and semen in males)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A farmer cultivates a unique species of tomato plants. The two traits selected for breeding were: colour of the fruits and height of the plants. The farmer initially crosses a homozygous tall plant bearing red fruits (TTRR) with a dwarf plant bearing yellow fruits (ttrr) and the genotype of all the offsprings of the F1 generation was TtRr. Next, he crosses two F1 generation plants (TtRr).
(a) Explain the phenotype of the offsprings of the F1 generation obtained from the initial cross.
questions.solution: All F1 plants are tall with red fruits, because tallness and red colour are dominant traits expressed in the heterozygous (TtRr) F1.

marking_points.point: All tall with red fruits, since tall and red are dominant (plants are heterozygous TtRr)

The farmer initially crosses a homozygous tall plant bearing red fruits (TTRR) with a dwarf plant bearing yellow fruits (ttrr) and the genotype of all the offsprings of the F1 generation was TtRr. Next, he crosses two F1 generation plants (TtRr).
(c) State Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.
questions.solution: In a dihybrid cross, the alleles of the genes of two characters separate at the time of gamete formation and then recombine independently to give new combinations.

marking_points.point: Alleles of two characters assort independently during gamete formation and recombine in new combinations
